questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

In the olden days, many __people use to think__ that the earth was flat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"people used to think"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "use to" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "used to" hence, the correct phrase is "people used to think."
 
• "used to" is a modal verb that shows past habits. (done or experienced in the past, but no longer done or experienced)
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• I used to eat meat, but now I’m a vegetarian.
 
 

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** *In the olden days, many** people used to think** that the earth was flat. *

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Arrest the thief.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Let the thief be arrested."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the Active voice and an imperative sentence.
 
• While changing the imperative sentence into the passive voice then, we have to follow the following structure-
 
 
• Let + object + be + past participle.
 
 
 
• For example-
 
 
• Active: Carry it home.

 Passive: Let it be carried home.
 
 

**So the correct passive voice is**-* Let the thief be arrested. *

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences which are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. It also wants to know how many students have been provided nutritious food and improved their overall health.

B. The Midday Meal Scheme, that aims to provide free food to children, is in focus again.

C. About 1.3 million government schools are covered under this welfare program of children.

D. The Government now wants to take stock of the implementation of the program.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "BCDA"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The passage talks about the "midday meal scheme".
 
• The first sentence will be **sentence B** as it tells that the Midday meal scheme.
 
• The second sentence will be **sentence C** as it further tells about the Midday meal scheme and how many schools are covered under this scheme.
 
• The third sentence will be **sentence D** as it tells what the government is doing.
 
• The fourth sentence will be **sentence A** what the government wants to know after the implementation of the program.

 

**So the correct sequence is-** ***B.** The Midday Meal Scheme, that aims to provide free food to children, is in focus again. **C. **About 1.3 million government schools are covered under this welfare program of children. **D. **The Government now wants to take stock of the implementation of the program.** A. **It also wants to know how many students have been provided nutritious food and improved their overall health.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Several minutes had passed / before she returned / carry milk / for the dog.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **"carry milk"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "carry" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "carrying"
 
• In the given sentence, there are two clauses the main clause and the subordinate clause. In the subordinate clause, i.e. "before clause" "returned" is the main verb and a transitive verb and we know that after the transitive verb we always need to use an object. 
 
• "carry" is a verb hence, we need to use a present participle form of this i.e. "carrying" so the main object will be "milk". "carrying" will tell about "milk".

**So the correct sentence is-** *Several minutes had passed before she** returned carrying milk** for the dog.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

“What is Sonia saying?” said Rohit.

options.text: Rohit asked what was Sonia saying.
Rohit asked that what was Sonia saying.
Rohit asked what is Sonia saying.
Rohit asked what Sonia was saying.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Rohit asked what Sonia was saying."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the case of** Interrogative **sentences like this, “said” in Direct Speech is changed into “enquired (of)”, “wanted to know”, “asked”, etc.
 
• In Indirect speech, the** verb** is always placed **after **the **subject**, unlike in direct speech.
 
• For example:
 
 
• The teacher said to him, “What is your name?” (Direct Speech)
 
• The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)
 
 
 
• Hence, 'is Soniya saying' is changed into 'Sonia was saying'. (verb is placed after the subject in the Indirect Speech).
 
• Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the **Present Continuous tense**. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the **Past Continuous tense**.

**So the correct sentence is**- *Rohit asked what Sonia was saying.*
